bull.b: Durable free cash flow and strong cash conversion (FCF ~90% of net income) provide operating flexibility to fund launches, trials, and partnerships without immediate refinancing. This reduces execution risk and supports reinvestment through product cycles over the next several quarters.

The company moved from multi-year losses to meaningful TTM profitability and healthy gross margins, indicating commercial economics can sustain earnings. If maintained, this supports funding of pipeline and reduces reliance on external capital over a 2–6 month horizon.

bull.t: Commercial execution: AMVUTTRA scale and TTR franchise growth
bull.b: Rapid AMVUTTRA traction and broad TTR adoption show durable commercial strength, expanding prescriber base and international expansion potential. High product revenue concentration is balanced by demonstrable scale and recurring demand supporting medium-term revenue stability.

bear.t: Meaningful leverage and prior balance-sheet volatility
bear.b: Although leverage has improved, a ~$1.27B debt load and a history of negative equity leave the capital structure more sensitive to earnings setbacks. Persistent leverage can constrain strategic flexibility and increase refinancing risk if cash generation slows over coming quarters.

bear.t: Gross margin pressure from rising royalty rates
bear.b: Rising average royalty obligations are a structural margin headwind as AMVUTTRA scales; lower gross margins reduce incremental cash generation on additional sales and magnify the impact of price declines or reimbursement pressures over the medium term.

bear.t: Increased R&D and SG&A investment pressures margins
bear.b: Elevated R&D and commercial spend is necessary for pipeline progression and market expansion but raises fixed-cost run-rate. If clinical or market outcomes disappoint, higher operating expenses could quickly compress operating leverage and earnings durability across the next several quarters.
